summary: Identity header whitespace normalization causes tenant claim mismatch and 401s in private deployment
description: Issue summary: Customers in MercuryHealth's private VPC started seeing sporadic 401s when invoking the Redwood inference API via their tenant-scoped service account. Impact: Affects several production endpoints serving ML-backed features for the customer; estimated 20-30% request failures for a subset of callers. Environment: Private deployment (MercuryHealth), prod-us-west region, ingress via on-prem edge proxy -> private-agent -> auth service. Steps to reproduce: 1) Authenticate via configured IdP (SAML) and obtain assertion. 2) Edge proxy forwards X-Identity-Principal header to private-agent. 3) Make API call with header present; observe 401 depending on caller. Observed behavior: Some requests fail with 401 Unauthorized. Logs show that tenant claim received by the auth service includes trailing spaces or collapsed internal spacing (e.g., "tenant:acme ") which does not match canonicalized tenant binding in RBAC cache ("tenant:acme"). Expected behavior: Header contents should preserve original claim encoding or the auth layer should canonicalize equivalent whitespace so tenant mapping succeeds. Logs and artifacts: - Edge proxy upgrade on 2026-03-09 has transform enabled: header normalization ("collapse-multiple-spaces=true"). - Sample header received at auth (raw): "X-Identity-Principal: user=svc-analytics; tenant=acme\n" - Auth service log: "rbac: lookup tenant 'acme ' -> no binding found -> 401" - Ingress proxy access log: 10.5.23.12 - - [09/Mar/2026:14:55:12 +0000] "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1" 401 123 "-" "svc-client/1.2.3" Temporary workaround: 1) Have the customer add a header transform in their edge proxy to strip trailing whitespace from tenant claim before forwarding (rules applied in their proxy config). 2) As short-term server-side mitigation, we've configured private-agent to accept a trimmed version of the tenant header for requests from MercuryHealth (feature-flagged).
investigation_notes: 03/10 09:18 - Support replicated issue in staging by enabling header normalization in test proxy and saw identical tenant mismatch behavior.
03/10 12:07 - SRE examined ingress proxy config and found recent gorouter 2.3.1 upgrade added a default header-normalization filter; upstream change note mentions collapsing whitespace.
03/11 03:40 - Auth team confirmed RBAC cache lookup is strict string match and does not currently trim or normalize claim values.
03/12 11:05 - Reproduced with cURL by injecting X-Identity-Principal header with trailing space; auth service rejected; trimmed header accepted.

Hypothesis: The edge proxy's normalization change is altering SAML-derived header payloads (trimming/ collapsing whitespace/newlines), creating non-canonical tenant strings that fail RBAC binding checks.
Telemetry: Added temporary logging to auth lookup to record raw/trimmed claim for further correlation. Collected 120 examples from MercuryHealth showing a consistent trailing-space pattern.
Risk assessment: High impact for customer production; change is limited to their private ingress so blast radius contained.
resolution_notes: 03/13 07:30 - Rolled out emergency workaround: private-agent feature-flag 'accept-trimmed-claims' enabled for MercuryHealth; 401 rate dropped to <1%.

Planned fix: (1) Patch ingress transform documentation and recommend IdP->proxy contract to avoid header normalization of identity claims; (2) Add canonicalization (trim + collapse internal multiple spaces normalization) in auth service before RBAC lookup with accompanying unit tests; (3) Backfill RBAC cache to include trimmed variant mapping for 48 hours post-deploy.
Release plan: auth canonicalization patch targeted for 2026-03-18 in internal patch release; private-agent default will not accept trimmed claims globally until after review and tests.
Follow-up: Create runbook entry and Confluence note to warn customers about proxy upgrades that enable header normalization filters.
Customer communication: Sent interim status and workaround steps via email and opened dedicated Slack huddle (#support -> @mercuryhealth).

root_cause: Ingress proxy header normalization (recent default change) altered tenant claim formatting (trailing whitespace/collapsed internal whitespace) leading to strict RBAC string-match failures in auth service.
